Prepared for Orbiz · Screen designs v1

Event Management — every screen, designed first

A new, standalone product for event organisers — built fresh, reusing the proven PowerAuction modules (registration forms, category & member pricing, vouchers, Cashfree payments, ticket and admin registrations) where they fit. Pilot event: SIGMA Fashion Fest, Kochi, January 2027 (Orbiz). Walk-in registration at the venue is covered in three channels — self-service link/QR, a staffed registration desk, and group-assisted entry — in screen 09.

Pilot SIGMA Fashion Fest · Kochi · Jan 2027 (dates TBC) Organiser Orbiz — Noufal Screens 11 designed Status Design preview — for Orbiz review

Sample data: every name, count, price and code on these screens is placeholder content to judge the layout — SIGMA's real dates, prices and programme are not final yet. The mocks are interactive: try the guest form, the voucher code WELCOME10, the booth floor plan, the gate scanner and the check-in gates screen (11).

How the screens connect

Two journeys run through the same registrations database — the guest journey before and during the fest, and the organiser journey behind it. On event day, the live board and the gate scanner sit on top of both.

What it does

The single source of truth for an event. The organiser creates their own categories — there is no fixed list — sets base and member prices, issues vouchers, and shapes the form.

Key elements

  • Member pricing — matched by mobile number against the organiser's member list; the same pattern as PowerAuction's member categories
  • Vouchers — % or fixed ₹, one event only, shared cap per code
  • Form builder — built-in fields plus custom fields, toggled per event
  • Approval toggle — on, and tickets show “Pending approval” (see screen 07)

Open item

Whether SIGMA's money must settle into Orbiz's own Cashfree account (per-event organiser account) decides one build item — flagged on the screen itself.

What it does

One form for every guest, rendered from the organiser's setup — fields, categories, prices and vouchers all come from screen 03, never hardcoded.

Key elements

  • Category cards with the price on the card — no surprises at payment
  • Member price — the member line appears only for the Buyer category; the discount is verified server-side by mobile number at payment

  • Fee is re-computed at payment, not trusted from the screen

What it does

The one screen a guest keeps. It has to work as a screenshot in a gallery, on WhatsApp, and at a crowded gate with poor light.

Key elements

  • Organiser brand first (Orbiz strip), event next, platform credit last — the order agreed for ticket screens
  • QR + EVNT-ID pair — scan it, or read the ID aloud to the gate's manual search
  • Two honest states — Paid, or Pending approval with the explanation outside the ticket artwork, so a screenshot can't be mistaken for a valid pass
  • WhatsApp group button shows to everyone who completed registration, including pending guests

Source

Adapted from the PowerAuction ticket (same branding order and ID discipline); the QR code itself is new — it drives screens 08 and 10.

08

On-site — Gate check-in scanner

Mobile · staffNew build

The gate volunteer's whole job on one screen: point, scan, admit. Built for sunlight, queues and bad networks. Press “Simulate a scan” a few times — the third scan is a duplicate, the fourth is a code that doesn't exist.

Gate A · Entry

Point at the guest's ticket QR — it reads in under a second

Processed at this gate212
No QR? Search by name, mobile or EVNT-ID →
Online · scans sync instantly. Works offline too — 0 scans queued.

What it does

Check-in and check-out for every ticket type — guests, exhibitor teams and speakers all scan the same way.

Key elements

  • Three result states — admitted (green), already scanned (amber, with the first scan's time and gate), not found (send to manual search)
  • Manual fallback is one tap away and lands on the same search as screen 02
  • Offline-first — scans queue on the phone and sync when signal returns; the queue count is always visible
  • One device per gate, signed in as the gate — no personal logins at a crowded entry

Source

Entirely new — QR scanning is the critical-path module in the plan and the first thing to dry-run before the fest.

For whole groups: the exhibitor, college coordinator or delegation lead hands over one list — paper, Excel or WhatsApp — and our team enters it. Each guest still gets their own registration ID and QR pass; member pricing and vouchers apply per guest, exactly as in the other channels.

Why three channels

  • Self-service link/QR — zero staff, works before the guest even reaches the desk
  • Registration desk — staff-run tablet at the entrance for walk-ins, cash payers and guests without a phone
  • Group-assisted — exhibitor teams, student groups and buyer delegations arrive as lists; entering them centrally avoids spelling errors and duplicate entries

The one rule

Channels are entry points, not separate systems. One form definition, one price book, one ID series, one list — a duplicate mobile number in any channel flags the existing registration instead of creating a second one.

Editing — Gate AApplies to scanner 08 + live board 10

Closing a gate locks its scanner and greys the gate out on the live board (screen 10). Guests already inside are unaffected — check-outs reroute to any Entry + exit gate.

What it does

The setup screen behind the scanner. A gate only exists — and a scanner can only sign in — once it is defined here, so the counts on the dashboard and live board always trace back to a named entry point with a named lead.

Key elements

  • Mode per gate — Entry + exit, Entry only, Exit only, or Registration + check-in for the desk; the scanner screen (08) inherits it
  • Staff & scanner assignment — a lead, the staff count and the paired devices per gate; unassigned gates stay closed
  • Open / closed control — closing a gate locks its scanner instantly and updates the live board
  • Counts match everywhere — Gate A 592, Gate B 326, Desk 36 are the same totals the live board (10) shows
  • Add gate — a new entry point starts closed and unassigned until staff and a scanner are set in the editor

Source

New — the companion to the gate scanner (08) and the live board (10). Those two screens already assumed gates existed; this is where they are created.

What is reused, what is new

A new codebase and a new product — but the registration core is the one already proven live on PowerAuction. Reuse is at module level: same behaviour, same edge cases handled, carried into the new project.

ModuleSourceNote
Registration form engine + custom fieldsReusePer-event form config, built-in + custom fields — screens 03, 06, 09
Categories & member pricingReuseOrganiser-created categories; member matched by mobile number; server-side fee quote — screens 03, 06
Voucher codesReuse% or fixed ₹, single event, shared cap per code — screens 03, 06
Payments (Cashfree)ReusePlatform account at launch; per-event organiser account is the open item on screen 03
Admin registrations + ID searchReuseSame EVNT-ID on ticket, admin and gate; search by name / mobile / ID — screen 02
Ticket success screenAdaptedSame branding order (organiser → event → platform) and WhatsApp group button; gains the QR — screen 07

Speaker schedulingNewDays, stages, sessions, speaker confirmation — screen 04
Booth alignmentNewZones, floor grid, exhibitor assignment, pass issue — screen 05
QR check-in / check-out + live boardNewGate scanner, offline queue, inside-now counts — screens 08, 10 · dry-run before the fest

Open points to confirm with Orbiz

Four details to lock together before the build starts — none of them changes the designs above except where noted.

POINT 1
SIGMA's exact dates
January 2027 is confirmed; the day(s) set the whole timeline backwards — registration live ~7 weeks before, check-in dry run ~2 weeks before.
POINT 2
Final categories & prices
Delegate, Buyer / Retailer, Student and Exhibitor team are placeholder categories in these designs — Orbiz confirms the final list, prices and member rules.
POINT 3
Payment settlement account
If SIGMA's registration money must land in Orbiz's own account, the per-event organiser payments module joins v1 (it's flagged on screen 03).
POINT 4
Badge printing at the desk?
The desk flow (screen 09) assumes a small printer at the entrance. If printing is out, passes stay QR-only and the desk screen simplifies.
